title: Important Amendments Related to FR, DPSP, and FD

blocks.content: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 ensured that the right to protection in respect of conviction for offenses and protection of life and personal liberty under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

rows: Gave precedence to all DPSPs over Fundamental Rights under Articles 14, 19, and 31.
Added four new DPSPs: Articles 39, 39A, 43A, and 48A.
Inserted Part IV-A containing 10 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.
Removed Right to Property (Art 31); protected Articles 20 & 21 from suspension during emergency.
Restored primacy of FRs over DPSPs except for Articles 39(b) and 39(c).
No direct changes made to Fundamental Duties.
Inserted Article 21A making free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 a Fundamental Right.
Substituted Article 45 to focus on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.
Added the 11th Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k) for parents and guardians.

items: Articles 20 and 21 can NEVER be suspended during a National Emergency as per the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
Right to Property was deleted from Part III by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and relocated as a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.
The 86th Amendment Act (2002) simultaneously impacted all three major sections: FR (Art 21A), DPSP (Art 45), and FD (Art 51A(k)).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) introduced Part IV-A and added 10 Fundamental Duties based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations.
The 44th Amendment Act (1978) removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
The 86th Amendment Act (2002) inserted Article 21A (Right to Education), modified DPSP Article 45, and added the 11th Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k).
The 25th Amendment Act (1971) gave precedence to Directive Principles under Article 39(b) and 39(c) over Fundamental Rights under Articles 14, 19, and 31.
